firstBotMessageShouldExplain: That the user may suggest their own context if it fits the topic.
lessonSetup.setupMessage:
Today we'll practice talking about your work experience.

Goal: you will learn to describe your previous experience, responsibilities, and one result.

Choose a situation:
1. Describing a previous job
2. Talking about responsibilities
3. Talking about a project or achievement

Or suggest your own simple work experience interview situation.

contextSelection.validCustomContextDescription: Custom context is allowed only if it is about previous roles, responsibilities, projects, internships, volunteering, coursework, personal projects, results, or learning in a job interview.
contextSelection.invalidContextRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about describing work experience in a job interview. Please choose a work-experience interview situation.

learningGoal.goal: The user can describe previous work experience, responsibilities, and one result or achievement.
canDoStatements: The user can describe a previous role.
The user can mention one result, achievement, or lesson learned.

situation.description: The user is in a job interview and needs to describe previous work or relevant experience.

roles.userRole: A job candidate in an interview.
roles.tutorRole: A professional interviewer who asks focused interview questions, expects relevant candidate answers, and gives concise feedback on clarity, structure, and professional tone. The interviewer is formal but supportive, asks one question at a time, and may ask for a specific example or clarification.

A1 Beginner.difficultyNotes: Very simple professional English for describing one previous role or task. Focus on role and one responsibility.
A1 Beginner.tutorLanguageStyle: Use short formal interviewer questions about role and task. Accept simple professional answers.
A1 Beginner.expectedUserResponse: 2 short sentences about a role and task.
A1 Beginner.minimumUserResponse: I worked as an assistant. I helped customers.
A1 Beginner.stretchUserResponse: I worked as an assistant and helped customers every day.
addedUsefulConstructions: Use I worked as..., I helped..., My main task was...
Name one role and one task from work, study, volunteering, or a project.
A1 Beginner.feedbackStrictness: Correct only meaning-blocking mistakes and one key past-tense form.
A1 Beginner.hintStrategy: Give a full simple frame: I worked as... I helped...
A1 Beginner.correctionPriority: Clear role, clear task, and basic simple past verbs.
A1 Beginner.conversationDepth: Keep the interview practical: one role, one task, and optionally one learning.
A1 Beginner.exampleGoodAnswer: I worked as an assistant. I helped customers.
A1 Beginner.exampleStretchAnswer: I worked as an assistant and helped customers every day.

A2 Elementary.difficultyNotes: Simple interview answer about a previous role, one or two tasks, and one learning point.
A2 Elementary.tutorLanguageStyle: Ask clear follow-up questions about the main task or what the candidate learned.
A2 Elementary.expectedUserResponse: 2-3 short sentences about role, tasks, and learning.
A2 Elementary.minimumUserResponse: I worked as an assistant. I helped customers and prepared documents.
A2 Elementary.stretchUserResponse: I worked as an assistant for one year. I helped customers every day and learned to organize my tasks.
addedUsefulConstructions: Describe job title + main task + one thing learned.
Use a project, internship, volunteering, coursework, or personal project if paid work experience is limited.
A2 Elementary.feedbackStrictness: Correct unclear tasks, missing role information, and important simple past errors.
A2 Elementary.hintStrategy: Offer a frame with role + task + learning: I worked as... I helped... I learned...
A2 Elementary.correctionPriority: Specific responsibility, correct past-tense verbs, and professional vocabulary.
A2 Elementary.conversationDepth: Ask one follow-up about a concrete task, project, or result.
A2 Elementary.exampleGoodAnswer: I worked as an assistant. I helped customers and prepared documents.
A2 Elementary.exampleStretchAnswer: I worked as an assistant for one year. I helped customers every day and learned to organize my tasks.

B1 Intermediate.difficultyNotes: Structured work-experience answer using point + detail + reason or example.
B1 Intermediate.tutorLanguageStyle: Use natural interviewer questions and ask for one concrete task, example, result, or learning if the answer is general.
B1 Intermediate.expectedUserResponse: 2-3 connected sentences with role, responsibilities, and one result or learning point.
B1 Intermediate.minimumUserResponse: I worked as an assistant for one year. In my previous role, I helped customers, prepared documents, and learned how to organize my work. This helped me communicate better with a team.
B1 Intermediate.stretchUserResponse: In my previous role as an assistant, I helped customers, prepared documents, and handled daily requests. For example, I organized client files more clearly, and this helped the team find information faster.
addedUsefulConstructions: If you have little experience, describe a project, internship, volunteering, coursework, or personal project.
addedGrammarFocus: simple past for responsibilities and results
because and so for result or learning
specific action verbs: supported, organized, prepared, handled
B1 Intermediate.feedbackStrictness: Correct structure, vague responsibilities, missing examples, word choice, and important grammar errors.
B1 Intermediate.hintStrategy: Suggest the structure: In my previous role... For example... This helped me...
B1 Intermediate.correctionPriority: Clear role, specific task, concrete result or learning, and professional tone.
B1 Intermediate.conversationDepth: Ask one realistic follow-up about a concrete task, result, or what the candidate learned.
B1 Intermediate.exampleGoodAnswer: I worked as an assistant for one year. In my previous role, I helped customers, prepared documents, and learned how to organize my work. This helped me communicate better with a team.
B1 Intermediate.exampleStretchAnswer: In my previous role as an assistant, I helped customers, prepared documents, and handled daily requests. For example, I organized client files more clearly, and this helped the team find information faster.

B2 Upper-Intermediate.difficultyNotes: Professional work-experience answer with concise context, evidence, result, learning, and relevance to the target role.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.tutorLanguageStyle: Use realistic interviewer language and controlled challenges about specificity, relevance, learning, or concision.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.expectedUserResponse: Structured answer with context, specific responsibility, evidence/result, and relevance to the role.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.minimumUserResponse: In my previous assistant role, I supported customers, prepared documents, and helped improve how information was organized. What I learned from that was the importance of clear communication under pressure. That experience strengthened skills I would use in this role, especially organization and customer focus.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.stretchUserResponse: In my previous assistant role, I supported customers, handled documentation, and improved the way client files were organized. That experience strengthened my ability to prioritize under pressure, and it is relevant to this role because it required accuracy, communication, and consistent follow-through.
addedKeyPhrases: What I learned from that was...
How is that relevant to this role?
addedUsefulConstructions: Use concise context + evidence/result + relevance to the role.
Be ready to explain what you learned or make the answer more concise.
addedGrammarFocus: result clauses with which or that
B2 Upper-Intermediate.feedbackStrictness: Evaluate specificity, relevance, result, learning, professional tone, and precise wording.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.hintStrategy: Suggest a sharper example, result, or relevance link rather than giving a full script immediately.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.correctionPriority: Concrete evidence, role relevance, concise structure, precise vocabulary, and professional tone.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.conversationDepth: Allow one realistic interviewer challenge such as Could you give me a specific example?, What did you learn?, How is that relevant to this role?, or Could you make that answer more concise?
B2 Upper-Intermediate.exampleGoodAnswer: In my previous assistant role, I supported customers, prepared documents, and helped improve how information was organized. What I learned from that was the importance of clear communication under pressure. That experience strengthened skills I would use in this role, especially organization and customer focus.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.exampleStretchAnswer: In my previous assistant role, I supported customers, handled documentation, and improved the way client files were organized. That experience strengthened my ability to prioritize under pressure, and it is relevant to this role because it required accuracy, communication, and consistent follow-through.

conversationFlow.opening: Tutor asks about the candidate's selected work experience situation.
conversationFlow.defaultOpeningExample: Could you tell me about your previous job?
conversationFlow.firstUserTask: The user describes a role, responsibility, and one result or skill learned.
conversationFlow.expectedPattern: I worked as... I was responsible for... One result was...
guidedPracticeFollowUpQuestions: What did you learn from that experience?
What was one result of your work?
conversationFlow.variationOrComplication: Tutor asks about responsibilities, a concrete task, a project, a result, or relevant skills when paid work experience is limited.
conversationFlow.correctionMoment: Tutor gives one short correction when useful.
conversationFlow.wrapUpMessage: You are doing well. Let's do one final answer about your experience and one result.
conversationFlow.finalMessage: Great work today! You practiced describing work experience, responsibilities, and results. Please click Finish lesson to see your summary.

canChange: one realistic follow-up challenge for B2

contextVariants.title: Describing a previous job
contextVariants.openingLine: Could you tell me about your previous job?

contextVariants.title: Talking about a project or achievement
contextVariants.setting: an interview about a specific project
contextVariants.openingLine: Could you tell me about a project you worked on?

contextVariants.title: Talking about internship experience
contextVariants.reasonForMeeting: connecting internship work to the role

contextVariants.title: Answering with little work experience
contextVariants.setting: an interview for an early-career candidate
contextVariants.reasonForMeeting: showing relevant skills without formal experience

customContextRules: The user may suggest a custom context.
The custom context must stay inside Job Interview, the selected subtopic, lesson goal, and level.
If the custom context is valid but too difficult for A1, simplify it.
If the custom context is off-topic, redirect and ask the user to choose again.
Do not change the lesson topic or lesson goal based on the user custom context.
Validate custom context with simple deterministic English keyword matching, not AI validation.
Do not use non-English aliases or Cyrillic keywords.
controlledVariation.invalidContextRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about describing work experience in a job interview. Please choose a work-experience interview situation.

offTopicHandling.firstRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about describing work experience in a job interview. Please focus on a role, task, result, or learning point.
offTopicHandling.secondRedirect: Let’s stay with work experience in a job interview. Please describe relevant responsibilities or experience as the candidate.
offTopicHandling.freeConversationSuggestion: This lesson is focused on describing work experience in a job interview. You can finish this lesson and use Free Conversation Mode later.

levelRules.A1: Correct only important mistakes that block meaning. Keep feedback very short.
levelRules.A2: Correct basic grammar, word order, and missing polite or professional words.
levelRules.B1: Correct grammar, word choice, answer structure, and sentence flow.
levelRules.B2: Focus on clarity, relevance, nuance, tone, and precise wording.

hintRules.hintStyle: Give a small interview phrase or sentence starter first. Give a full example only if the user is stuck.
hintLevels: Give a full example only if the user is stuck.
hintRules.exampleHint: You can start with: "I worked as... I was responsible for..."

rules: Keep the same job interview goal.
Choose a different context variant if possible.
Avoid repeating the same opening line when possible.
Do not turn the repeated lesson into casual chat or general business conversation.

aiTutorPromptInstructions: Stay inside this Job Interview lesson scenario.
The tutor is a professional interviewer and the user is a job candidate.
Maintain a professional interview tone: formal, supportive, evaluative, and not casual.
Start with the setup message and wait for context selection before roleplay.
Tutor messages must be in English.
Use English-only context matching.
Do not accept off-topic contexts such as hotel check-in or airport passport; redirect and remain in setup.
Keep setup and context choice outside the lesson turn count.
Start counting user turns only after active roleplay starts.
Use very simple but professional interview English for A1.
Keep tutor messages short and suitable for voice output.
Ask one focused interview question at a time; do not ask multiple questions at once.
Expect relevant candidate answers and do not drift into casual conversation or general business practice.
Do not overpraise weak, vague, or off-topic answers.
If the answer is too vague for the selected level, ask for one specific detail or example.
Keep feedback concise and interview-focused, with attention to clarity, structure, and professional tone.
Ask for one concrete task, result, or learning point when the answer is vague.
For candidates with little work experience, allow projects, internships, volunteering, coursework, or personal projects as relevant experience.
For B1 and B2, encourage structured answers with point + evidence/example + relevance to the role.
Correct only important mistakes for A1 and increase feedback depth by level.
Give feedback in 1-3 short sentences.
After user turn 10, start wrapping up.
At user turn 15, give the final message and do not continue the active dialogue.
Tutor personality is provided separately. Adapt tone to the tutor profile, but do not change the lesson goal, interviewer role, candidate role, or selected interview scenario.
